en: The Jātaka:
The Section of Sevens,
Chapter on the Hen.
10. The Bakajātakasutta:
“Seventy-two are the karmas of merit, O Gotama, by which those who exercise mastery have transcended birth and old age.”
“This is the final attainment of Brahman for the one who has realized the truth;
this is what many people pray for from us.
“For this is but little, not a long life.”
“O Baka, as for that long life which you imagine—
O Brahmā, I know your lifespan to be a hundred thousand nirabbudas.”
“I am the Blessed One of infinite vision,
who has transcended birth, old age, and sorrow;
what use have I for former vows or conduct?”
"Explain to me that which I should know.
"That which you caused to be drunk by many people who were thirsty, exhausted by the heat; [that is what you ask]."
I recall that ancient practice of yours, like one awakened from sleep;
how you took hold of the people on the banks of the Eṇī river.
I released the one being led away as a captive;
I remember that former practice of vows and virtue of yours,
just as one who has woken from sleep remembers a dream.
A boat seized upon the current of the Ganges by a fierce nāga who had assumed human form—
you released it, overcoming him with your might.
That ancient practice of yours, your conduct and observance,
I remember as one awakened from sleep.
And I was your attendant for an eon.
I remember you as one possessed of perfect wisdom, observing vows and free from conceit;
I recall that ancient practice of yours in vows and virtue,
just as one who has woken from sleep remembers a dream.
“Truly you understand this lifespan of mine;
you know even more, for you are a Buddha.
For such is the blazing power of your majesty.”
“Shining, he stands in the Brahma-world.
The *Bakajātaka*, the tenth.
The First Chapter: The Chapter on the Cock.
Its summary verse:
Varakaṇṇika, Cāpavara, Sutana,
then Gijjha, Sarohita, and Macchavara.
Furthermore, Paṇṇaka, Senaka, Yācanaka,
and then Veri with Sabrahmabaka— these are the ten.
